item.description: Abstract Offshore freshened groundwater (OFG) is a significant yet underexplored component of the global water cycle, and its spatial distribution, particularly its links to past glacial processes, remains poorly constrained. The southeastern North Sea, characterized by extensive tunnel valley networks, provides an ideal setting to test how Pleistocene meltwater shaped offshore groundwater systems. Using newly acquired time-domain controlled-source electromagnetic data integrated with high-resolution seismic reflection surveys, we present a resistivity-based mapping of OFG in this region. The models reveal a laterally continuous OFG body with resistivities of 8–14 Ω·m, extending across multiple stratigraphic units and well beyond individual subglacial landforms. This configuration is best explained by subglacial meltwater flushing of sediment porewaters during Pleistocene glaciations. Subsequent preservation was aided by density contrasts that limit vertical mixing and by fine-grained glaciomarine deposits sealing the system from above. The connection between resistivity anomalies and mapped subglacial landforms shows that the latter can serve as predictive proxies for OFG occurrence. These findings shift the perspective from OFG as isolated anomalies to regionally extensive systems linked to glacial processes, establishing subglacial landforms as a testable screening proxy for locating OFG in formerly glaciated margins worldwide. item.description: Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability. Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation. item.description: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group. item.description: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins. item.title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau

item.description: Vegetation greening and abrupt permafrost thaw are reshaping sediment dynamics across the Tibetan Plateau, yet their relative effects on sediment delivery remain poorly quantified. Here we show that retrogressive thaw slumps are disproportionately important sediment sources, with erosion rates two to three orders of magnitude above undisturbed landscapes and source-to-channel connectivity generally exceeding 60%. Combining multi-decadal satellite observations, high-resolution topographic differencing and cold-region hydrological modelling, we quantify the competing effects of thaw-slump sediment supply and greening-induced erosion reduction. During 2000–2022, thaw slumps delivered more than four times as much non-ice sediment to channels as was reduced by greening, compensating for declining glacier-derived sediment and contributing to increased downstream suspended sediment export. Across permafrost regions, approximately 1.2‰ thaw-slump coverage represents an upper-bound threshold above which thaw-slump sediment delivery exceeds greening-induced sediment reduction. These results show that spatially limited abrupt thaw can outweigh widespread vegetation recovery in regulating sediment delivery from warming permafrost landscapes. Abrupt permafrost degradation through retrogressive thaw slumps can increase sediment delivery to Tibetan rivers, outweighing the greening-induced reduction in sediment export, suggests a study combining multi-decadal satellite observations, topographic differencing, and hydrological modelling. item.title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
item.dc:creator: Nathalie Casas
Guilhem Mollon
Marco Maria Scuderi
item.description: Earthquake nucleation is governed by the evolution of fault zone structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking grain-scale processes to macroscopic weakening remain elusive. Here we use discrete element simulations of quartz-rich gouge in which angular grains fragment dynamically, revealing a robust strain–damage law in which damage accumulates as grains are consumed. Grain size dictates the geometry and timing of localization, while fragmentation enhances compaction and promotes the emergence of a dominant Principal Slip Zone (PSZ). As comminution approaches a saturation state (i.e. minimum grain size), localization can migrate to competing bands, providing a mechanical explanation for overprinted shear fabrics in experiments and natural faults. By linking fragmentation, porosity evolution, and the resulting shear localization, our results provide a local fragmentation state variable for constitutive laws that couple grain-size evolution to fault weakening and the conditions for earthquake nucleation. This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation. item.description: K–Ar dating reveals >110 Myr of episodic Altyn Tagh Fault activity, beginning at ~115 Ma along a Cretaceous lithospheric weakness. Reactivation at ~56 Ma records rapid India–Asia collisional stress transmission >1500 km into the continental interior. The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict. item.title: Nickel isotopes in Apollo and Chang’e soils reveal widespread micrometeorite-driven processing of the lunar regolith
item.dc:creator: Ke Zhu
Maosheng Yang

item.description: Abstract Micrometeorite bombardment is a fundamental surface process on the Moon and other airless bodies, driving elemental evaporation, isotopic fractionation, and material mixing in surface regoliths. Here, we report high-precision stable Ni isotope data for lunar soils returned by the Apollo (11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17) and Chang’e (5 and 6) missions, covering geographically and geologically diverse lunar terrains. The analyzed soils show δ 60/58 Ni values of 0.345‰ to 1.280‰ (relative to NIST SRM 986), generally heavier than lunar basalts and the inferred bulk silicate Moon, indicating widespread heavy Ni isotope enrichment during surface processing. Together with published Chang’e-5 drill-core data, these results demonstrate that micrometeorite-driven Ni isotope fractionation is widespread across the lunar surface. Local variability, however, reflects additional controls. The relatively low δ 60/58 Ni values of the immature Apollo 12 soils are consistent with limited cumulative micrometeorite processing, whereas the mature Apollo 16 soils have high Ni concentrations and Ni/Co ratios, indicating additional compositional overprinting by Ni-rich material. Stable Ni isotopes, particularly when combined with regolith maturity and Ni/Co ratios, therefore provide a sensitive tracer of micrometeorite-driven lunar surface processing and its local overprinting. item.description: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. Here, we report noble gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe) isotope ratios in peridotite, pyroxenite, and eclogite xenoliths from the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton, Brazil. Helium isotopes reveal a strong radiogenic component, while neon shows MORB-like and nucleogenic signatures. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0–5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. This study reveals that noble gas isotopes in mantle rocks beneath the São Francisco Craton, Brazil, record the recycling of volatiles from Archean subduction into the continental mantle. item.description: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle. item.description: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain. item.description: Abstract The Jiaodong gold province, with proven resources of more than 5,700 tonnes, is the largest gold-producing region in China. Lamprophyres represent relatively primitive mantle-derived magmas that mainly experienced fractional crystallization, whereas the monzodiorites and MMEs represent more evolved magmas that underwent variable degrees of crustal contamination and magma mixing. Chalcophile element geochemistry indicates that sulfide segregation during lamprophyre magma evolution was limited. Consequently, the Au concentrations of the lamprophyres closely reflect the primary Au contents of their parent magmas (0.24–2.34 ng/g). In contrast, the evolved monzodiorites and MMEs experienced significant sulfide segregation and contain lower Au concentrations (0.05–0.60 ng/g). item.description: As one of the most important tectonic units in orogenic belts, the identification and evolutionary history of Japan-type island arcs are of great significance for understanding the formation and evolution of orogenic belts. Provenance analysis of (meta-)sedimentary rocks indicates that the accretionary complex units of the western Mongolia Collage System (the Hovd Terrane, Mongolian Altai, and Chinese Altai) share identical provenance characteristics. Synthesis of magmatic, sedimentary, structural, metamorphic, anatectic, geochemical, isotopic geochemical, and geochronological data from both regions reveals the simultaneous development of large-scale extension during the Late Silurian-Early Devonian. Integrating previous studies, we propose that during the Late Silurian-Early Devonian, large-scale slab roll-back triggered rifting of the fore-arc accretionary complex in front of the western Mongolian micro-continents. The rifted portion became the basement of the Chinese Altai, with the subduction zone remaining in front of the Chinese Altai. As subduction continued, a new oceanic basin opened behind the Chinese Altai arc. During the Middle Devonian-Early Carboniferous, this newly formed back-arc oceanic basin initiated subduction beneath the western Mongolian micro-continents, while subduction beneath the Chinese Altai arc continued throughout this period. item.description: The circum-Rodinia suprasubduction system maintained a dynamic equilibrium between extension and convergence along the periphery of the Rodinia supercontinent during its breakup. Although recent paleomagnetic data place the Yangtze Block at this margin, it remains unclear whether the Tonian tectonothermal events on its western edge are fully consistent with this configuration. This study examined a composite intrusive batholith of the Pengguan Complex on the western Yangtze margin, South China, comprising diorite, tonalite, granodiorite, biotite granite, and K-feldspar granite; however, a systematic synthesis of its properties for reconstructing the regional setting remains uncertain. Zircon U-Pb geochronology yielded consistent ages of ca. 801–794 Ma, representing the multiplex magmatic record of the western Yangtze Block during the middle Tonian. The various lithologies exhibit distinct zircon Hf-isotopic compositions, whole-rock geochemistry, Sr-Nd isotopes, and mineral geochemistry, reflecting partial melting at different levels across a continental-arc lithospheric profile. Diorite crystallized from an evolved hydrous magma ultimately related to a metasomatized mantle source, as evidenced by its arc-type trace element signatures and variable Nd-Hf isotopes. Tonalite and granodiorite display adakitic features, including elevated Sr/Y and (La/Yb)N ratios and reduced Ni and Cr concentrations, plus erratic Nd- and Hf-isotopic signatures. These features favor their derivation from partial melting of a thickened mafic lower crust. Distinct petrogenetic processes contributed to the formation of the biotite granite and K-feldspar granite, both of which are associated with transcrustal recycling. The former shows variable Nd- and Hf-isotope ratios derived from the reworking of ancient crust. In contrast, the latter has depleted Nd and Hf isotopes and younger model ages, resulting from partial melting of relatively juvenile lower-crustal components. These pieces of magmatism collectively represent multilevel partial melting of compositionally distinct domains in the mantle wedge and continental crust. The multilevel partial melting recorded by the studied batholiths in the Pengguan Complex within a continental arc setting, coupled with coeval Tonian subduction-related magmatism along the western Yangtze margin, constitutes a thermal manifestation of the convergent regime at the periphery of the Rodinia supercontinent during the early Neoproterozoic. item.description: Cobalt (Co), a strategic critical metal, is significantly sourced from magmatic CuNi sulfide deposits. The Jinchuan deposit, the world's third-largest magmatic CuNi sulfide deposit, provides an ideal setting for studying Co enrichment. Previous studies on Co enrichment have focused on isolated stages without quantitative comparison of their relative contributions, leaving the dominant mechanism unresolved. This study analyzed ore types (massive, net-textured, and disseminated) from drill core ZK50–3 in Segment II, employing petrography, SEM-EDS, and EPMA to elucidate the distribution, occurrence states, and enrichment mechanisms of Co. Results show that Co primarily resides in pentlandite via isomorphous substitution for Fe2+ and Ni2+, with selective fluid alteration causing anomalous enrichment in secondary magnetite and pyrite. Two key enrichment stages are identified: sulfide liquid segregation (enrichment factor: 39–43) and fractional crystallization of the sulfide melt (enrichment factor: 172–189), with the latter playing a dominant role. This study provides the first quantitative comparison of their relative contributions to Co enrichment. The high-Mg tholeiitic parental magma, relatively enriched in Ni but depleted in Co, was generated by low-degree partial melting of peridotite within a metasomatized, enriched subcontinental lithospheric mantle. During cooling of the sulfide melt, Co preferentially entered the monosulfide solid solution (MSS) and subsequently migrated into pentlandite at 450–550 °C. The presence of pyrite and magnetite with elevated Co concentrations can provide useful exploration clues for CoNi mineralization. In particular, Co-rich hydrothermal magnetite particularly acts as a diagnostic indicator of intensive fluid overprinting. This work elucidates occurrence and enrichment of Co, offering insights for both ore genesis and mineral exploration. item.description: The Lavra Velha deposit in the São Francisco Craton (Bahia, Brazil) is an iron sulfide-copper–gold (ISCG) system. item.description: The Triassic platform carbonates of the Eastern and Southern Alps host over 500 Pb-Zn deposits collectively known as Alpine-type (AT) Pb-Zn deposits. The AT deposits represent a subclass of Mississippi Valley–Type systems and one of Europe’s largest provinces for base and strategic metals (e.g. Ge, Ga) resources. Despite their importance, the source of metals, timing of mineralization, and mechanism driving fluid flow in the province remain debated. The Raibl deposit (Italy) displays structural and mineralogical features typical of the class, making it an ideal site to investigate controls on Pb-Zn accumulation. This study provides the first, detailed petrographic and compositional characterization of the hydrothermal carbonates associated with the Pb-Zn mineralization at Raibl and present in-situ U-Pb ages on syn- to post-ore carbonate domains alongside new Pb isotopic data on galena from Raibl and other selected AT deposits. Syn-ore carbonates show a distinctive geochemical signature (Fe and Mn enrichment) and constrain the mineralization to a short interval in the Late Triassic (214.0 ± 5.8 Ma to 205.2 ± 3.3 Ma). These constraints support a revised genetic model involving Late Triassic mobilization of oxidized, metal-bearing brines sourced from Permian clastic units (i.e. Val Gardena Sandstone and the Sesto Conglomerate) during early regional extension and strike-slip tectonic. Epigenetic sulphide precipitation at 2–4 km depth resulted from in-situ reduction of these fluids through interaction with organic-rich, Late Triassic lithologies. The proposed model for Raibl aligns with evidence from the world-class Bleiberg deposit but contrasts with smaller mineralized AT systems (e.g. Gorno) that record Middle Triassic, shallow diagenetic mineralization. Overall, the results suggest diachronous fluid flow and metal deposition across the province, emphasizing the role of local structural and geochemical factors in controlling economic accumulation of base metals. item.description: S-type granites are far less abundant during much of the Archean than in the Phanerozoic, and this paucity remains puzzling. We propose that the suppression of S-type granite formation at scale may have been an inherent consequence of the hotter Archean crust. A key insight from fossil P-T-t paths in representative orogens is that the onset of melting can trigger exhumation and thereby limit the maximum burial depth of sediments.​ In a hot crust, this maximum burial depth is relatively shallow, because hot geotherms initiate melting at shallow depths due to the pressure dependence of dehydration melting. By contrast, colder geotherms in Phanerozoic orogens effectively suppress melting until higher pressures and temperatures. As a result, Archean sedimentary packages were exhumed too early to undergo extensive decompression and dehydration melting attainable in modern cycles. Phase equilibria modeling shows that the exhuming metasediments in the Archean may only generate melt fractions 1/3 to 1/2 of those in the Phanerozoic. Such low melt productivity in the Archean may have inhibited the formation of large S-type plutons and batholiths. More broadly, these processes may have impeded deep recycling of sediments and, by limiting upward distillation of heat-producing elements, slowed the cooling of the Archean continental crust. item.description: The world-class Bayan Obo REE-Nb-Fe deposit in North China is the world’s major source of rare earth elements (REEs) and second largest niobium (Nb). item.description: Early Earth’s primordial crustal record has been largely modified and reworked by subsequent tectonic processes, particularly during the onset and evolution of plate tectonics, although remnants of early crustal domains may still be preserved in some terranes. item.description: Sapropelic cryptocrystalline graphite (SCG) occurs in an Early Cambrian rift-platform setting of the South Qinling Orogenic Belt. Nevertheless, the mechanisms of its graphitization and its genetic evolution remain poorly constrained. In this study, we systematically investigated the petrology, geochemistry, and genesis of SCG using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and carbon-isotope analysis. The results indicate that SCG and its host rocks occur predominantly in the Cambrian Shuigoukou Formation and Yuejiaping Formation. The associated mineral assemblage comprises quartz, calcite, chlorite, muscovite, phengite, pyrite, and garnet. SCG is characterized by a high degree of graphitization (84–98%) and a high ash content. Graphite crystallites have lateral dimensions of 28–86 nm, stacking heights of 21–30 nm, and interlayer spacings (d 002) of 0.3355–0.3368 nm. Geochemical proxies indicate that the carbonaceous protolith was deposited in a reducing nearshore, shallow-marine setting, with contributions from terrigenous clastic materials and seafloor hydrothermal inputs. Sapropelic organic matter likely represented an important carbonaceous component of the protolith. The δ13CVPDB values of the SCG samples range from −29.84‰ to −19.61‰, consistent with a predominantly biogenic organic-carbon source. Raman geothermometry yields Raman-derived graphitization temperatures of 487.2–513.8 °C. Muscovite and phengite occur mainly as the 2 M1 polytype, with b0 values of 0.9006–0.9047 nm, indicating a medium-pressure metamorphic environment. Combined with regional metamorphic constraints, the estimated pressure–temperature conditions of 0.58–0.79 GPa are consistent with greenschist-facies metamorphism. These results suggest a two-stage evolutionary process involving (1) the accumulation and preservation of organic-rich carbonaceous sediments under reducing marine conditions during the Early Cambrian and (2) subsequent tectono-metamorphic graphitization during regional deformation and metamorphism. Hydrothermal fluid activity, deformation, and mineral matter may have further influenced the graphitization process and contributed to the formation of SCG. item.description: As one of the most pivotal continental blocks in Southeast Asia, the South China Block (SCB) hosts globally significant ore systems and serves as a natural laboratory for studying intracontinental polymetallic mineralization. To constrain its deep lithospheric structure, this study constructed a 3-D lithospheric electrical structure model using magnetotelluric (MT) data from the Qianjiang-Fuzhou Line, a 700-km-long, NW-trending profile with 51 stations. The model reveals pronounced multi-scale heterogeneity in the lithospheric electrical structure, characterized by distinct vertical stratification and lateral discontinuity. A total of eight conductive anomalies (C1-C8) and six resistive anomalies (R1-R6) were identified through the analysis. The Yangtze Block is characterized by high resistivity (>103 Ω·m) as the dominant feature, while the eastern Cathaysia Block contains several prominent crustal-scale conductors (C6, C7, C8) overlain on moderately resistive lithospheric mantle (102-103 Ω·m). In general, the crustal conductors in the eastern SCB support the interpretation of lithospheric dehydration-induced thermal erosion. This process facilitated the ascent of deep-sourced fluids through Late Mesozoic magmatic channels into the upper crust, thereby enhancing crustal conductivity and establishing effective crust-mantle material exchange. Such spatial correspondence between lower-crustal conductors and lithospheric thinning zones further reinforces this mechanism. Meanwhile, our findings align best with a dynamic model tied to the Meso-Cenozoic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific Plate. The tectonic sequence involves initial lithospheric thickening during flat-slab subduction, subsequent large-scale asthenospheric upwelling during slab rollback, and final regional extension and lithospheric thinning driven by slab break-off. This tectonic evolution fostered the formation of a rejuvenated lithosphere and extensive magmatic-minerogenetic systems, while further controlling regional metallogenic distribution through large-scale crust-mantle interactions that remelted both ancient and juvenile crust. In addition, translithospheric fault systems act as conduits for asthenospheric materials and fluid circulation, directly regulating the spatial distribution and metal assemblages of major ore belts to reflect variable shallow responses to deep dynamic processes.
